messages:
paul (support): FYI customer ACME (tenant: acme-42) opened a support escalation — their p95 jumped after the runtime/version rollout we started last night. They see text.generate p95 ~600ms -> ~1.2s and increased error rate 0.2%->0.7% since 03/15 canary
marie (sre): thanks. do we have a cohort id or request examples? any trace ids from their payloads?
devin (runtime): got the flag — ACME cohort = cohort-acme-42. I can pull logs if someone drops the trace ids. my first guess is kernel selector or scheduler change in v2026.03.15 that affects small short sequences (auth path + small prompts).
paul (support): attached sample request and one trace id in the ticket: trace=fd12ab34. sample input: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-7b",
  "input": "Summarize:\n- short bullet list",
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```
marie (sre): pulling dashboards now — grabbing p95/p99 per-cohort and per-node. linking grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency/serving?cohort=cohort-acme-42 :eyes:
devin (runtime): looking at canary vs stable: canary has slight increase in kernel-select avg latency for short seqs. There was also a small quantization change in the build that touched the fast-path.
ahmad (oncall): can we repro in staging with a replay of ACME traffic? if yes we can bisect. I'll queue a synthetic replay now. command: `./replay --tenant acme-42 --sample 2000 --target staging`
runtime-bot: Replay job queued -> job-id=rep-20260315-77. estimated run: ~12m. will post results.
ops-bot: Canary cohort routing: cohort-acme-42 currently 20% canary, 80% stable per rollout config v2026.03.15.
marie (sre): interesting — p95 on the canary nodes spikes and tails widen on nodes with kernel v2.3; stable nodes with kernel v2.2 look fine. could be scheduler change interacting with KV cache coldness.
devin (runtime): hypothesis: scheduler introduced slightly longer slot waits for tiny batches which increases p95 for short-response flows. mitigations: 1) reduce canary weight for cohort-acme-42 to 0% 2) enable fallback to stable kernel for that cohort 3) force-prefetch KV cache for that tenant 4) bisect commit range to find offending change.
paul (support): ACME is asking for temporary mitigation now. they want either rollback or traffic pinned to stable.
ahmad (oncall): I recommend immediate traffic steering for ACME -> pin to stable (ops-bot can do) and keep canary reads disabled. if replay reproduces, we will plan a fast rollback.
ops-bot: Changing routing: cohort-acme-42 weight -> 0% canary (applied). Confirmation: traffic now routed 100% to stable cluster for cohort-acme-42.
runtime-bot: Replay finished. summary: p95 on staging canary = 1.18s, stable = 0.62s. repro successful. job logs: 
```
rep-20260315-77: 2000 reqs, p50=120ms, p95_canary=1180ms, p95_stable=610ms
sampling: high fraction of short sequences affected
```
devin (runtime): ok repro confirmed. next step: bisect the runtime commits between v2.2 -> v2.3. I'll start binary search across commits that touched scheduler + kernel selection + quantization flags. expecting to find one of the small scheduler tweaks.
marie (sre): while devin bisects, let's enable two quick mitigations for production: 1) per-tenant KV prewarm for acme-42 (reduces cold-start tails) 2) enable 'latency-guard' guardrail that prefers stable kernels for requests under 128 tokens. both are low-risk. can someone run the prewarm script?
ahmad (oncall): running prewarm: `./tools/prewarm_kv --tenant acme-42 --pool 10`
ops-bot: prewarm job started -> prewarm-889. ETA 4m.
devin (runtime): bisect started. checking mid commit: revert of scheduler backoff patch yields p95 drop in staging. marking candidate commit: 9f3b2c (scheduler: refine backoff for tiny batches).
marie (sre): great. can we hotfix to tune that backoff rather than full rollback? might be faster for a patch.
devin (runtime): I can assemble a hotpatch that reverts backoff change but keeps other fixes. build/test takes ~10m. if green we can roll to canary and monitor.
paul (support): ACME has been notified that traffic pinned to stable and we're doing hotpatch/rollback. they appreciate the quick action.
ahmad (oncall): action items: devin -> produce hotpatch PR + quick canary; marie -> monitor cohort telemetry and confirm p95 drops; paul -> keep customer updated; ops -> keep routing pinned until we see stable p95.
runtime-bot: hotpatch build queued -> build=hotpatch-20260315-21.
marie (sre): temporary note: record this under postmortem tracking id PM-2026-0315-acme-latency for follow-up evals. we'll run regression tests for short-seq workloads and add a synthetic test for cohort-sized KV warming.
devin (runtime): hotpatch built and deploying to canary for 10% traffic for non-ACME cohorts first, then we'll widen.
ops-bot: canary deploy of hotpatch started.
marie (sre): after hotpatch: canary p95 for short seqs down to 660ms (from 1180) on staging. not as low as stable but big improvement. request to prod: can we route acme back to canary 10% to validate?
ahmad (oncall): recommend keep ACME on stable until we see prod metric improvement for a few minutes. we'll coordinate gradual reintroduce.
paul (support): told ACME we expect another update in 30m after validation. they asked for postmortem when resolved.
marie (sre): logging final state here: cohort pinned to stable, prewarm in place, hotpatch deployed to canary, bisect points to commit 9f3b2c, follow-up: regression test, add canary gating for scheduler backoff changes.
devin (runtime): closing loop: PR #4521 created to revert backoff tweak with test coverage. tagging marie/ahmad for rollout plan.
paul (support): closing ticket pending postmortem. will update ACME once we merge and schedule rollback/hotpatch rollout if needed. :white_check_mark:
